prospects.thesis: Leidos combines a defensive government-services backlog with growing exposure to defense IT, AI-enabled mission systems, and cyber — all tailwinds under sustained DoD and civil agency budgets. At just 1.0x P/S with a $17.8B cap and +33% 1M momentum, it offers scale at a reasonable valuation, and bullish options plus institutional flow confirm smart money accumulation. Near-term catalyst: continued task-order awards under recent IDIQ vehicles and margin expansion in the Health/Digital segment.

SMCI is the leading builder of AI-optimized servers and liquid-cooled racks tied directly to NVIDIA Blackwell/GB200 shipments, giving it direct leverage to hyperscaler AI capex. At just 0.7x P/S with a $25.7B cap after +43.7% 1M momentum, valuation remains reasonable versus revenue trajectory, and bullish options + institutional flow suggest a re-rating is underway following its audit/compliance cleanup. Catalyst: FY26 revenue guide and Blackwell rack ramp into H2.

MongoDB's document database and Atlas Vector Search are becoming a preferred backend for AI/RAG applications, driving reacceleration in Atlas consumption. +35.3% 1M with bullish options and institutional support suggests the AI workload narrative is finally translating to durable ARR growth after last year's stumble. Catalyst: next earnings print showing Atlas net-new workload growth and enterprise AI pipeline conversion.

AVAV is the pure-play leader in small unmanned aerial systems (Switchblade loitering munitions, Puma UAS) — a category with exploding demand from Ukraine lessons-learned, Replicator initiative, and Indo-Pacific drone stockpiling. +34.1% 1M momentum with bullish institutional flow reflects the BlueHalo acquisition expanding it into space, C-UAS, and directed energy. Catalyst: Replicator Tranche 2 awards and FY26 backlog updates.

GitLab's Duo AI assistant and end-to-end DevSecOps platform monetize the AI-coding wave with a differentiated single-application approach versus GitHub Copilot's fragmented stack. At 6.9x P/S with a $7.0B cap, it's the most reasonably valued AI-software name on this list, and +23% 1M with bullish options/institutional signals indicates the Duo attach rate story is gaining traction. Catalyst: Duo Enterprise seat expansion and federal/regulated-industry wins on self-managed deployments.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Here's what's interesting: the biggest bullish bets are piling into Real Estate and Utilities — the two most interest-rate-sensitive sectors on the board — which tells me big money is positioning for rate cuts or at least a Fed that's done hiking, and it lines up with the bond market too (LQD, investment-grade bonds, is flashing bullish). Tech is quietly bid as well, which fits the "soft landing plus AI capex" narrative, and there's likely an assumption that whatever tax and deregulation talk is floating around Washington keeps the mega-cap growth trade alive. On the flip side, the aggressive hedging in Materials (that 49x put/call is genuinely wild) and Industrials suggests smart money is bracing for tariff blowback, a China slowdown, or the reality that infrastructure spending is peaking — basically, they don't believe the "reflation" story the cyclicals have been telling. Healthcare getting sold hard is almost certainly about drug pricing pressure, Medicare negotiation expansion, and election-year political risk that nobody wants to own into headlines. The contradiction to watch: HYG (junk bonds) is flashing bearish while LQD is bullish and credit spreads are widening — that's a classic "flight to quality" setup where the market is quietly separating winners from losers even as the index looks calm, and it usually precedes a month or two of defensive leadership and choppier price action. The non-obvious takeaway most headlines are missing: this isn't a "risk-on" rotation, it's a *duration* rotation — people are buying long-dated cash flows (utilities, REITs, quality bonds) and dumping economically-sensitive stuff, which means the smart money is betting the economy cools faster than the Fed or the White House is admitting, and they're front-running the pivot rather than the boom.
